skillSays: Treat colour as a system, not a pick: build ramps in OKLCH so lightness steps are even across hues, then clamp chroma to the gamut instead of letting it clip.
Layer tokens as reference (raw palette), semantic (surface, text, brand, accent, error) and component use, and encode decisions (hover, tints) as derivations rather than hand-picked hex.
Use native CSS colour features first: oklch(), color-mix(in oklab), relative colour syntax, light-dark(), and gradients interpolated in OKLCH so they do not go grey in the middle.
Check every text and background pair with WCAG and APCA in both light and dark, and keep tints neutral-tinted rather than pure grey.
Proportion the palette (60-30-10), prefer character (muted, vivid, deep) over hue-wheel rules, and compute a complement from the actual colour's OKLCH hue instead of a colour name.

changes: Generated sea, coral, neutral, red and green ramps (50 to 950) in OKLCH with gamut-clamped chroma and tinted the grey ramp toward the brand hue, instead of picking a few hex values by eye.

Took the accent from the brand's actual OKLCH hue plus 180 degrees (sea 222, coral 42) and kept it to roughly 10% of the page: dots, one underline and the open-slot marker; teal surfaces carry the other 30%, neutrals the 60%.

Hero gradient is interpolated in OKLCH, the hover state is color-mix(in oklab) of the brand with the text colour, and translucent washes use relative colour syntax, so nothing has a second hard-coded hex.
Verified 26 text and surface pairs in light and dark with both WCAG and APCA, and changed the tertiary text step after one pair failed 4.5:1.
The recommended plan is separated by a brand-tinted OKLCH gradient and brand border, while coral appears only on the Most popular flag and the savings pill, so the accent stays rare.
Text on the coral flag uses the near-black neutral (4.8:1) rather than white, because the skill says to check the pair, not assume it.
Dark mode swaps through light-dark() on the semantic tokens, so every card, price and check icon follows without separate dark rules.
Error styling is a semantic pair (red text on a red-tinted background, both checked at 6:1 or more in both modes), plus a 3px ring derived from the error colour with relative syntax.
Control borders use the tertiary text step (4.5:1) so inputs stay visible, rather than a faint decorative line.
The page backdrop is an OKLCH gradient from the brand tint into the neutral surface, which stays clean instead of turning grey mid-way.
